problem: Hospitals lack real time operational decision support for patient flow, surgery scheduling and capacity.

founders.name: Mudit Garg
founders.background_notes: Qventus team page confirms co-founder; prior employers and schools not found in opened sources.

founders.name: Ian Christopher
founders.role: Co-founder and Chief Engineer (also shown as CTO)

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed real time hospital data integration and predictive models in a regulated environment.

defensibility.rationale: Deep integration with hospital systems and long enterprise sales cycles.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition; remained independent through a 2025 Series D.

market_need_then: Hospitals faced capacity and throughput pressure; awards in 2016 and 2017 (Fierce, Healthcare Informatics) reflect demand per YC page.

rebrands.why: Not found in sources; former name appears in a Crunchbase link label on the YC page and one profile

brand_strength.rationale: Enterprise brand recognized by KLAS and awards but little evidence of brand as growth driver.

outcome_analysis: Qventus sold operations software to hospitals, raised a 30 million Series B in 2018, a 50 million growth round in 2022 and a 105 million Series D led by KKR in January 2025. Enterprise sales to health systems and integration lock in drove steady growth, and it remains independent.
notes: The article on the 2018 round states over 43M total raised, more than the rounds recorded, so earlier rounds exist. An aggregator lists a 13M Series A in November 2016 (Norwest, Mayfield) and a 2015 round, unverified. Series D reported as 105M including 85M equity and 20M optional debt by one outlet. Totals range 98M to 216M across aggregators. Competitors found were present day vendor lists, none dated near 2015, so list empty.
